755: Lead time, freight, belt, incline, installation, parts and technical service: the most common questions about conveyors, screw conveyors, elevators and packing.
756: How do I request a quote?
757: By WhatsApp, phone, e-mail or any form on the website. To speed things up, tell us the material conveyed, the distance to cover, the discharge height and the capacity you want. If you can send a photo or video of the site, the sizing will be more accurate.
758: What is the manufacturing lead time?
759: It depends on the equipment and on the production queue when you order. The lead time is confirmed in writing in the proposal and followed by the same specialist who served you. Meeting deadlines is a commitment of ours: when something changes, we tell you beforehand.
761: Yes. The factory is in Limeira/SP and we deliver across the whole country, with logistics followed by our team until the machine arrives. For other countries, talk to our export team.
762: Do you serve individuals and small operations?
763: Yes. We serve everyone from farmers and small agro-industries to large plants. The equipment is sized for the scale of the operation, without pushing a bigger machine than you need.
765: Freight is quoted together with the proposal, according to the destination and the dimensions of the equipment. You can use our quote or your own carrier.
767: The terms are presented in the commercial proposal, including the options for orders with down payment and for invoicing. We issue an invoice for every order.
768: Do you take part in purchasing processes and supplier registration?
769: Yes. We send the company documentation for supplier approval and take part in quotation processes of industries, cooperatives and integrators.
770: Is it possible to visit the factory?
771: Yes, and we recommend it. Seeing the cutting, welding, painting and testing process helps you understand our manufacturing standard. Arrange the visit with the sales team by WhatsApp.
772: Which belt should I use for each material?
773: Bags and boxes call for a smooth belt; loose material going uphill calls for a cleated belt, so the load does not roll back; fine bulk performs better on a V belt, which forms a trough; a food line calls for a non-toxic belt that is easy to sanitize. When in doubt, describe the material and we will recommend one.
774: What is the maximum incline of a conveyor?
775: It depends on the material and on the belt. Packaged product on a smooth belt accepts a gentle incline; above that, cleats are needed to hold the load. Loose grain slides before baled material does. The final angle is defined in the project, together with the discharge height.
776: How do I know the capacity I need?
777: Start from the volume per hour your operation needs to move at peak, not on average. Capacity comes from the combination of belt width, speed and profile type. Our calculator gives a starting point and engineering confirms the model.
778: Do you build in stainless steel and for food lines?
779: Yes. We build stainless steel versions and versions with sanitary belts for operations that require sanitation, as well as galvanized versions for harsh environments.
781: Yes, and it is a large part of what we build. Z conveyors, big bag hoppers, structures on rails, specific elevations and adaptations of length, width and incline to fit your layout.
783: We work with drives compatible with the power supply available at your plant, including three-phase. Tell us the site voltage in the quote request so the motor leaves the factory correct.
784: Is it possible to vary the conveyor speed?
785: Yes. In sorting and checking operations adjustable speed makes a difference, because the conveyor's pace has to match the team's pace. This is defined in the drive.
786: Does the equipment have safety guards?
787: The machines are built with guards on moving parts and can receive the devices your operation requires. Tell us your plant's safety requirements in the quote request.
788: Does the machine arrive ready to use?
789: Nothing leaves the factory without a running test. Larger equipment may arrive in parts for transport and is assembled on site following the guidance we send along.
790: What do I need to have ready before delivery?
791: Free floor space, a firm and level floor, a power point at the correct voltage, enough headroom and access for unloading the truck. Each product page has the installation sheet with these items.
792: Do you provide installation and training?
793: We provide installation and operation guidance for your team. For larger projects, we assess on-site support. Agree on it when closing the order.
795: We have our own technical service and a direct channel to open a request. When it can be solved with remote guidance, we solve it; when a part or a visit is needed, we arrange it.
797: Yes. Belt, rollers, scraper, bearings, gearbox, motor and bag sewing items. Keeping wear parts in stock avoids line stoppages during harvest.
798: What maintenance does the machine require?
799: A simple routine: daily inspection of belt and scraper, weekly check of tension and alignment, and lubrication and bearing review in the monthly plan. Each product page has the checklist, and there is a PDF to print and hang in the factory.
801: All equipment has a factory warranty, with the conditions described in the proposal and in the delivery documentation. Natural wear of consumable items, such as the belt, is not covered.
802: Do you service older Demakine equipment?
803: Yes. We refurbish and recover our equipment, including belt replacement, structural reinforcement and drive replacement.
